task_read: This is an extreme long-horizon build: a from-scratch Excel-clone product (persistent server + REST + WebSocket collab + vanilla SPA + a 100+ function Excel-365 formula engine with dynamic-array spilling, dependency-graph dirty recompute under perf budgets, XLSX/CSV round-trip against a held-out LibreOffice oracle, plus pivots, defined names, conditional formatting, locale input, validation, iterative calc, and goal seek). The exact wire contract is deliberately under-specified in prose and must be reverse-engineered from the first-party client at /dev_tests/helpers.py, and grading is a large HIDDEN suite. This task warrants near-maximal, sustained meta-work across every dimension: deep contract orientation, layered milestones over a vast surface, self-built verification against Excel semantics, continuous progress tracking, and constant course-correction — plus strategic allocation of finite effort across breadth vs. depth.

dimensions.name: Contract & environment reconnaissance
dimensions.description: Reverse-engineering the exact wire shapes from /dev_tests/helpers.py and probing the environment (available libs, run.sh, Excel/LibreOffice semantics) before and while building, instead of guessing the API from prose.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec explicitly says the true wire contract (ids, cell shapes, patch/fill/sort/filter bodies, kind discriminator, spill fields, listing envelope) is 'whatever helpers.py already calls into.' Guessing instead of reading it guarantees systematic mismatch with the hidden suite; the prose alone is insufficient.

anchors.0: Starts implementing endpoints purely from the prose; never opens helpers.py or run.sh; invents field names.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once for a couple of endpoints, then builds mostly from prose; misses the discriminator/spill/envelope details.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py to pin down the core cell/workbook/patch shapes and runs run.sh early to see what the smoke suite expects before coding those paths.
anchors.8: Systematically extracts the full contract from helpers.py (every request body, cell kind incl. spill ghosts, spill_range, error names, listing envelope), cross-references it against prose to resolve ambiguities, and probes the environment (installed libraries for OOXML/formula I/O, openpyxl readability constraints) before committing to an approach.
anchors.10: Maintains a living, evidence-based model of the contract: re-consults helpers.py whenever a new feature surface is touched, infers underspecified Excel semantics (spill/#SPILL!, criteria wildcards, LWW-by-seq, locale canonicalization) from authoritative reasoning rather than assumption, and proactively identifies contract corners the smoke suite doesn't exercise but the hidden suite likely will.

dimensions.name: Layering a vast surface into checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the enormous feature surface into an ordered dependency-respecting hierarchy (bootable server+health+persistence → cell model → dependency/recompute → formula engine → dynamic arrays/spill → I/O → collab → SPA → analyst surface → iterative/goal-seek), each with an explicit done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With dozens of interdependent subsystems and hard foundations (persistence, dependency graph) that everything else builds on, an undifferentiated push collapses. Sequencing and per-milestone done-criteria are what keep the build coherent over a very long horizon.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between random features (e.g. pivots before the cell model works); no notion of 'done' per piece.
anchors.3: A flat undifferentiated to-do list that ignores dependencies and lacks per-item completion criteria.
anchors.5: A sensible ordered plan that establishes foundations first (bootable server, health, persistence, core cell CRUD) before layering features, with rough milestones.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone hierarchy where each milestone names how it will be confirmed done (e.g. 'recompute topo-order verified on a 3-cell chain before adding functions'), and later features are deliberately deferred until their prerequisites pass.
anchors.10: A milestone structure that also encodes risk and coupling: foundational/high-leverage subsystems (dep graph, spill materialization, XLSX round-trip) are sequenced first and gated by concrete checks, cross-cutting invariants (WebSocket cells payload == REST patch shape) are called out as shared milestones, and the plan is revised as real dependencies surface rather than followed rigidly.

dimensions.name: Self-built correctness checks beyond the smoke suite
dimensions.description: Deliberately designing checks that go past the non-exhaustive /dev_tests suite: validating formula results against known Excel semantics, exercising spill/#CIRC!/error propagation, confirming XLSX openpyxl-readability and value round-trip, and testing perf budgets and persistence-across-restart.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The spec warns the smoke suite is non-exhaustive and grading is a hidden suite with a LibreOffice ground-truth oracle. Assuming 'run.sh passes' means correct is the dominant failure mode; correctness of 100+ functions and round-trips must be independently established.

anchors.0: No verification, or only eyeballing; never runs run.sh.
anchors.3: Runs run.sh and treats a green smoke suite as proof of correctness; no independent checks of function values or edge cases.
anchors.5: Runs the smoke suite plus a handful of own spot-checks on core formulas, persistence-after-restart, and the health endpoint.
anchors.8: Builds targeted checks the smoke suite doesn't cover: representative formulas per function family validated against known-correct Excel outputs, spill/#SPILL!/#CIRC! and error-propagation cases, XLSX exports re-opened with openpyxl to confirm named ranges/formats/styles/CF survive, and explicit perf checks against the stated budgets.
anchors.10: Establishes an independent correctness oracle and uses it systematically — e.g. cross-checking evaluated values against real Excel/LibreOffice reasoning across many functions and locales, round-trip differential tests (export→import→compare, REST-vs-WebSocket payload parity), adversarial edge cases (occupied spill targets, iterative-calc convergence, goal-seek non-convergence), and treats any discrepancy as a signal to dig rather than a nuisance — verification depth scales with the breadth of the surface.

dimensions.name: Tracking done-vs-remaining across a huge feature matrix
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which of the many subsystems/functions are implemented, working, or broken, and detecting stuck/circular states (e.g. repeatedly re-debugging one formula) across a very long build.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is large enough that it's easy to lose the plot — believe a feature is done when it regressed, or sink disproportionate time into one function while dozens go untouched. Accurate status tracking is what sustains progress to the finish.

anchors.0: No sense of overall state; forgets whole feature areas; no detection of being stuck.
anchors.3: Vague mental tracking; rediscovers unfinished areas late; keeps retrying the same failing approach without noticing.
anchors.5: Keeps a working checklist of major features and updates it as pieces land, catching obvious gaps before wrapping up.
anchors.8: Maintains a live, granular status of subsystems and function families (done / partial / failing), re-runs prior checks to catch regressions as new code lands, and notices when it's thrashing on one problem to redirect effort.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate horizon-wide picture that drives decisions: explicitly reconciles claimed-done against re-verified-done, detects circular debugging early and changes tactic, budgets remaining effort against the still-uncovered surface, and avoids both premature 'finished' declarations and rabbit-holes.

dimensions.name: Course-correction when semantics or perf diverge
dimensions.description: Revising design, approach, or library choices when reality contradicts assumptions — Excel-semantics mismatches, spill/dependency bugs, perf-budget misses, or XLSX/openpyxl incompatibilities — rather than pressing on with a falsified plan.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many parts are subtle (dynamic-array spilling, dirty-only topo recompute under tight budgets, iterative fixed-point calc, OOXML that stays openpyxl-readable). First designs will be wrong somewhere; the ability to detect and re-architect is what separates a working product from a stuck one.

anchors.0: Ignores contradicting evidence; keeps a broken approach; ships on a falsified assumption.
anchors.3: Makes only local patches around symptoms (e.g. special-casing one failing formula) without questioning the underlying design.
anchors.5: When a check fails, diagnoses and fixes the real cause for that feature, and adjusts nearby plans accordingly.
anchors.8: Treats surprising failures as signals about the design: e.g. reworks the recompute/dependency model when perf budgets are missed, or the chosen OOXML approach when openpyxl can't read the export, and updates the plan to reflect the new understanding.
anchors.10: Repeatedly and cheaply re-architects when warranted: recognizes a foundational assumption is wrong early (before it contaminates dependent features), weighs alternative strategies against evidence, migrates approach decisively, and re-verifies the affected surface — converting divergence into durable design improvements rather than accumulating hacks.

dimensions.name: Coverage-maximizing effort allocation
dimensions.description: Strategically allocating finite effort across a surface far larger than can be perfected, to maximize expected hidden-suite coverage — trading breadth (many function families / endpoints minimally working) against depth (a few done flawlessly).
dimensions.why_it_matters: The catalog and feature list are enormous and grading is a broad hidden suite; a practitioner who perfects one corner while leaving whole families unimplemented scores worse than one who gets broad coverage working and then deepens high-value areas. This portfolio judgment is specific to this task's structure and isn't captured by sequencing alone.

anchors.0: Pours all effort into one narrow area (e.g. perfecting pivots) leaving most of the surface unimplemented, or spreads so thin nothing works end-to-end.
anchors.3: Follows the spec top-to-bottom without regard to payoff, running out of horizon with large high-value areas untouched.
anchors.5: Consciously prioritizes getting core, high-frequency surface working broadly before niche features, giving reasonable coverage.
anchors.8: Makes explicit breadth-vs-depth calls tied to likely graded weight — securing broad end-to-end coverage of common functions/endpoints first, then deepening high-value or high-risk areas — and consciously time-boxes low-payoff rabbit holes.
anchors.10: Runs a deliberate, evidence-informed portfolio: estimates where hidden-suite value concentrates, sequences to lock in broad coverage early, revisits allocation as time is spent, and cuts or defers low-yield perfectionism to redirect effort toward the highest marginal coverage — maximizing graded outcome under the horizon constraint.
